why: Azure sells general and GPU instance families directly, so the rental reset is first order for the cloud segment.
condition: Cloud segment revenue growth moves with the g5 and g5g rental change before total revenue does.
falsifier: Segment revenue growth is insensitive to those family prices.
test: segment revenue against lagged g5 and g5g monthly change

why: AWS sells the same families and also the Trainium and Inferentia lines that substitute for them.
condition: Rental change reaches AWS revenue growth with the substitute mix held visible.
falsifier: AWS revenue growth moves with its own price cuts rather than market rental prices.
test: segment revenue against lagged family prices and own price announcements

why: Google Cloud sells GPU families and TPUs, so the substitution matters more than the level.
condition: Rental change reaches Google Cloud revenue only where TPU substitution is limited.
falsifier: Revenue growth tracks TPU capacity additions instead.
test: segment revenue against family prices and TPU disclosure dates

why: Meta is a buyer of capacity, not a seller, so the transmission runs through cost and the external sale of surplus.
condition: Rental change reaches Meta's reported cost of revenue and its surplus capacity sales.
falsifier: Cost of revenue is insensitive to rental prices because capacity is owned outright.
test: cost of revenue against lagged family prices

why: OCI sells large training clusters, so the high end families are the relevant ones.
condition: Rental change at the high end reaches OCI revenue growth.
falsifier: OCI revenue growth is set by contract backlog alone.
test: segment revenue and backlog against lagged high end family prices

why: A dedicated GPU cloud, so nearly all revenue is directly levered to rental prices.
condition: Revenue per megawatt moves with the rental change for the families sold.
falsifier: Revenue is set by multi year contracts and does not track spot rental resets.
test: revenue per megawatt against lagged family prices

why: Mines bitcoin and rents GPU capacity, so the mix decides how much of the rental change lands.
condition: The GPU share of revenue grows and tracks rental prices.
falsifier: Mining revenue swamps the GPU line for the whole window.
test: segment split against lagged family prices

why: Sells powered capacity and hosting, so the lever is contracted revenue per megawatt.
condition: Revenue per megawatt rises with rental prices at contract renewal.
falsifier: Revenue per megawatt is fixed by signed leases for the whole window.
test: revenue per megawatt against family prices at renewal dates

why: Converted mining sites hosting compute, so the same revenue per megawatt lever applies.
condition: Hosting revenue per megawatt tracks rental prices with a contract lag.
falsifier: Revenue is flat per megawatt across the window.
test: hosting revenue per megawatt against lagged family prices

why: A colocation REIT sells power and space, so the lever is rent per megawatt and power pass through, not GPU families.
condition: Rent per megawatt per renewal rises with power and capacity tightness rather than GPU rental prices.
falsifier: Rent per megawatt tracks GPU family prices one for one.
test: rent per megawatt against the capacity tightness measures already in the graph
